premises.text: Data demand now exceeds what computing can handle because servers overheat and slow or drop under load

premises.text: Two-phase cooling (liquid to gas) can go below ambient/room temperature unlike today's air or water cooling
premises.evidence_span: The difference from air cooling or water cooling that's used today, this can allow us to go below ambient. That means we can go below room temperature, and there is no cooling system in the market that can do that today

premises.text: Company's in-cooling server is a standard form-factor drop-in for existing data centers with two-phase cooling inside
premises.evidence_span: this is our server. It's a standard server. You can insert it in any data center today, so you don't have to change a thing. And inside is our magic cooling system

premises.text: Lower CPU temperatures accelerate compute and improve energy efficiency (claimed ~50% less time and half the energy)
premises.evidence_span: By going lower on the CPU, we both accelerate it, so we make it go faster, and we can actually make it more energy efficient
